tool_summary: Sends a signal to processes matched by name or other attributes rather than by PID. Pattern-based targeting means a broad or loose pattern can affect far more processes than intended.
platform_notes: pkill is present on both GNU/Linux (procps) and macOS/BSD; core flag semantics (-9, -f, -u) are consistent for the purposes of this ruleset.

rules.description: A very short or generic pattern (e.g. a single common letter, or a wildcard-like substring) combined with pattern matching can match and signal many unrelated processes rather than the one intended.
rules.reversible_note: -f matches against the full command line rather than just the process name, widening the match surface; whether this is dangerous depends heavily on the specific pattern used, which commandant does not further evaluate for specificity.

rules.description: SIGKILL (-9 or -KILL) terminates matched processes immediately without allowing them to clean up, flush buffers, or release resources gracefully.

Sends a signal (SIGTERM by default) to all processes matching the given name pattern. Unlike kill, the affected process set depends on runtime pattern matching against currently running processes, not a fixed PID.
